original_line_97: The two 4-cells from `a` to each of the three high sets give eight high-sector words, filling the binary cube at `A=a`. Each pair among the synchronized parties is `D`: a `Q` pair cannot have support only `H x H` plus `L x L`, because its two high cells form a matching and cannot account for all four high-high cells implied by each high symbol's two neighbors and synchronization. Equivalently, synchronization gives all four high-high values, each with multiplicity three. The cube supplies two extensions of each such value; the remaining four high words form a parity code. For any high symbol of any synchronized party, its two non-`a` words use one `A` symbol, because its degree toward `A` is two. The incidence graph of the parity code through its three coordinates is connected, so all four words have the same `A` symbol `b`. The cube at `a` plus the parity slice at `b` exhausts the `4,2` values on pairs containing `A` and the four multiplicity-three values on complementary pairs. The isolated-block criterion gives a contradiction. Thus **three synchronized 4-alphabet parties cannot coexist with a 3-alphabet fourth party**.                         (5.1)
